reuse.why: The existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend is extended and reused for the move rule at all three sites, but the new daily-skip and holiday-skip rule is not put in it and is re-expressed by hand in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange.

duplication.why: The predicate `!isWeekend(date) && !isHoliday(date, holidays)` for daily skipping, plus the over-fetch-then-filter logic, is written three times with different look-ahead sizes (7+holidays, count*2+holidays, ±holidays+2 days), and getNextDate repeats it for the reverse fallback.

placement.why: isHoliday and the moving loop sit correctly in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-schedule rule lives in the server handlers and in getNextDate instead of in the shared weekend definition, and schedule-template never applies it.

scope.why: Edits stay on the schedule date path, types and tests, with only the parseRecurDate pass-through of holidays outside it, which the feature needs.

maintainability.why: A future change to the weekend/holiday rule for daily schedules has to be made in three places with different heuristics, and the budget-template path already disagrees with them because it never skips daily weekend occurrences.

bypasses_abstraction.where: app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (isDaily branch skips getDateWithSkippedWeekend and filters on its own), shared/schedules.ts getNextDate daily filter.

disguised_duplication.where: Daily-skip filtering is restated in getNextDate (take 7+holidays, plus the reverse fallback), getUpcomingDates (take count*2+holidays then slice) and getDatesInRange (window padded by holidays+2 days, isDaily branch); same rule in a different shape each time.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains skipWeekend and holidays params; the daily-skip rule bypasses it in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and schedule-template.ts does not apply it at all.
